questions.q: What gap does Lesson 8's scheduled refresh close that Lessons 3-7 left open?
options: Athena queries were broken without a schedule
The ETL job didn't actually produce correct data until this lesson
Redshift couldn't store the data until a schedule was added
Everything worked, but only when someone manually started each step — nothing ran on its own
questions.explain: Finance asked for numbers that update on their own; every prior lesson's piece still required a human to trigger it.

questions.q: What does the EventBridge Scheduler rule northfield-nightly-refresh target?
options: Starting the Glue crawler northfield-raw-crawler
Running the Redshift COPY statement directly
Sending a notification email to Finance
Starting the Glue job northfield-orders-etl on a daily cron schedule
questions.explain: The rule's cron(0 5 * * ? *) schedule starts northfield-orders-etl at 5 AM UTC; the Redshift load is a separate downstream step.

questions.q: Why is northfield-load-trigger configured as a CONDITIONAL trigger watching for SUCCEEDED, rather than firing on its own independent timer?
options: CONDITIONAL triggers are the only type Glue supports
A timer-based trigger could start the Redshift load before the curated data has finished writing, loading stale or partial data
It makes the ETL job run faster
It avoids needing an IAM role for the load job
questions.explain: Watching for SUCCEEDED specifically means the load only ever starts once there's correct, complete curated data to load.

questions.q: What kind of Glue job is northfield-redshift-load, and why that type?
options: A streaming job, because it processes data continuously
A Python Shell job, because it just issues a SQL COPY command with no large-scale Spark transformation needed
A container-based job, because it runs a custom Docker image
A Spark job, because it reprocesses the entire raw dataset
questions.explain: There's no transformation left to do at this step — just re-issuing the Lesson 5 COPY statement, which fits a lightweight Python Shell job.

questions.q: What real capability does this lesson's design deliberately leave for the Advanced tier?
options: Structured failure handling, alerting, and orchestration of a longer branching chain (Step Functions / CloudWatch)
The ability to query Redshift from Athena
Storing data in S3 in Parquet format
The ability to run the ETL job at all
questions.explain: A schedule plus one conditional trigger removes the 'someone has to run this' problem, but doesn't give retries, branching, or alerting — that's the Advanced tier's job.
